subject: AcmeTech onboarding: benchmark runbook and acceptance check
messages:
From: Alex Morales <alex.morales@acmetech.io>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: SRE Team <sre@acmetech.io>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: AcmeTech onboarding: benchmark runbook and acceptance check

Hi Olga and Redwood team,

Thanks again for the demo last week — AcmeTech is ready to move to the formal onboarding benchmark. We have two primary acceptance goals: average 95th-percentile latency <= 180ms for single-question lookups, and sustainable throughput of ~350 qps during 30-minute steady-state.

Attached is our internal run template (acmetech-loadplan-v1.xlsx) and a short list of dataset slices we want to include. High-level asks:
- Confirm Redwood's preferred load pattern (open vs closed) and whether the KV cache warmup should be included in the 30-minute window.
- Can you run an initial smoke load this week and share basic telemetry (tail latencies, CPU/GPU utilization, token counts)?
- We will provide a signed MPA/PO within 48 hours after we reach acceptance.

Availability: SRE and I are flexible Wed/Thu PST afternoons. Suggest Wed 3pm PST for the smoke.

Alex
Alex Morales
Head of Infrastructure, AcmeTech
---
Attachment: acmetech-loadplan-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morales <alex.morales@acmetech.io>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: AcmeTech onboarding: benchmark runbook and acceptance check

Alex — thanks for the clear targets. Happy to run a smoke and then a full acceptance run. Quick notes from our side:

1) Load pattern: we recommend a closed-loop test with a fixed number of virtual users to match your expected concurrency; that gives the most reproducible throughput for LLM services. We can provide both open and closed patterns if you prefer to compare.
2) KV cache: for the acceptance window we typically exclude initial warmup from the 30-minute steady-state, but we record end-to-end runs including warmup in the artifact bundle so you can see delta behavior.
3) Telemetry: we'll share tail latency (p50/p90/p95/p99), throughput, GPU utilization, memory pressure, token breakdowns, and request/response sizes.

Proposed schedule:
- Wed 11 Feb 2026 15:00 PST — smoke (15 min) to validate the harness and baseline.
- Thu 12 Feb 2026 10:00 PST — 30-min acceptance run (steady-state window excludes warmup).

I've looped in Monica (on implementation) and Ben (performance lead). Can you confirm Wed/Thu times? Also link to our runbook and the HubSpot deal: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1AaB-example-runbook and https://app.hubspot.com/deal/ACME-1398.

Thanks,
Olga
Olga Petrov
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Morales <alex.morales@acmetech.io>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: SRE Team <sre@acmetech.io>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 13:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: AcmeTech onboarding: benchmark runbook and acceptance check

Olga — Wed 3pm PST works for the smoke; Thu 10am PST is fine for the acceptance run.

Two clarifications from our SRE lead:
- Traffic mix: we will include 70% short queries (single-turn lookups), 30% multi-turn prompts (average length 120 tokens).
- Auth / certs: we will need a temporary API key and the TLS fingerprint for your ingestion endpoint for mutual TLS validation before Thu run.

I'll share a small onboarding checklist this evening with IP allowlist entries.

Alex

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morales <alex.morales@acmetech.io>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 08:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: AcmeTech onboarding: benchmark runbook and acceptance check

Alex — thanks, we'll provision a scoped API key for the smoke run and record the TLS fingerprint tonight. Ben and I will own the harness configuration (Irene will support telemetry ingestion). Quick checklist items we will complete before Wed 15:00 PST:
- API key (scoped to load harness) and mTLS fingerprint: provisioned and shared in secure note.
- Test dataset uploaded to our staging bucket (we will confirm S3 URI).
- Load script parameters: VUs=80 closed-loop, think-time=70ms, average token length per request set per your split.

Ben will post the final run parameters in the shared drive and include the k6 script and raw metrics format. Expect a smoke artifacts bundle (logs + short summary) within 1 hour after Wed's run.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morales <alex.morales@acmetech.io>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 16:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: AcmeTech onboarding: benchmark runbook and acceptance check

Alex / SRE team — attach is the acceptance artifacts bundle from today's run. Summary highlights:
- Steady-state window (30m) achieved average throughput = 358 qps; p95 latency = 172 ms; p99 = 305 ms.
- GPU utilization averaged 68% across the pool; no OOM events.
- KV cache warmup effects: p95 during first 5 minutes peaked to ~280 ms, then stabilized below 180 ms for the steady window.
- Failures: 2 transient 500s (root cause: downstream embedding store throttling), both retried successfully by harness.

Attachments: run-1-summary.csv (CSV), run-1-telemetry.zip (profiles + logs). Full artifact bundle uploaded to Drive: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1AaB-example-runbook

Next steps proposed by Redwood:
1) We recommend one additional acceptance run with the short/multi-turn split inverted (30/70) to ensure multi-turn tail behavior meets your SLAs.
2) We will prepare a short acceptance packet for your legal/procurement team showing SLO snapshots and the incident log for the failed requests.

If these outcomes look good to you, Olga can coordinate the procurement signoff and we will schedule the final corroboration run.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Performance Lead, Redwood Inference
